title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Anti-Subsidy Administrative Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 2 Any individual or organization having a legal interest in the countervailing administrative act shall be an interested party and may, in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations, institute an administrative action with the People's Court.
The interested parties referred to in the preceding paragraph shall mean the applicant who has submitted a written application for a countervailing investigation to the competent authority under the State Council, the relevant export operators and import operators, and other natural persons, legal persons or other organizations having a legal interest.

Article 3 The defendant in a countervailing administrative case shall be the competent department of the State Council that has taken the corresponding countervailing administrative act complained of.
Article 4 Other competent departments of the State Council that have a legal interest in the countervailing administrative act complained of may participate in the proceedings as a third party.

Article 6 The People's Court shall, in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations on countervailing measures, and with reference to the departmental rules of the State Council, conduct a legality review of the factual and legal issues of the countervailing administrative act complained of.

Article 7 The defendant shall bear the burden of adducing evidence for the countervailing administrative act complained of that it has taken, and shall provide the evidence and the regulatory documents on the basis of which the countervailing administrative act was taken.
The People's Court shall examine the legality of the countervailing administrative act complained of on the basis of the administrative record of the defendant.
Factual materials that were not recorded in the administrative record at the time the defendant took the countervailing administrative act complained of shall not serve as the basis for finding that act lawful.

Article 8 The plaintiff shall have the responsibility to provide evidence for the facts it asserts.
If, after examination by the People's Court in accordance with legal procedures, the evidence provided by the plaintiff is relevant, lawful and authentic, it may serve as the basis for adjudication.
If, during the countervailing administrative investigation procedure, the defendant, in accordance with legal procedures, requests the plaintiff to provide evidence, and the plaintiff, without justifiable reasons, refuses to provide it, fails to provide it truthfully, or otherwise seriously obstructs the investigation, and then provides evidence during the litigation proceedings, the People's Court shall not admit such evidence.

Article 9 Where, during the countervailing administrative investigation procedure, an interested party, without justifiable reasons, refuses to provide evidence, fails to provide evidence truthfully, or otherwise seriously obstructs the investigation, the factual conclusion drawn by the competent authority of the State Council on the basis of the evidence that can be obtained may be deemed as having sufficient evidence.
Article 11 The People's Court may, when hearing a countervailing administrative case, refer to the provisions concerning procedures for foreign-related civil actions.

Article 12 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2003.
November 21, 2002
